answer_text:
# Finding the Minimum Number of Die Throws

## Setting Up the Problem

Let $m$ be the number of times "one" appears in $n$ throws. Then $m \sim \text{Binomial}(n, p)$ with $p = 1/6$.

The condition is:
$$P\!\left(\left|\frac{m}{n}-\frac{1}{6}\right|\leqslant 0.01\right) \geqslant P\!\left(\left|\frac{m}{n}-\frac{1}{6}\right|> 0.01\right)$$

Since these two events are complementary, this simplifies to:
$$P\!\left(\left|\frac{m}{n}-\frac{1}{6}\right|\leqslant 0.01\right) \geqslant \frac{1}{2}$$

## Normal Approximation

The binomial variables are:
$$E[m] = \frac{n}{6}, \qquad \text{Var}(m) = n\cdot\frac{1}{6}\cdot\frac{5}{6} = \frac{5n}{36}, \qquad \sigma_m = \frac{\sqrt{5n}}{6}$$

The inequality $|m/n - 1/6| \leqslant 0.01$ becomes:
$$\left|\frac{m - n/6}{\sigma_m}\right| \leqslant \frac{0.01\,n}{\sqrt{5n}/6} = \frac{0.06\,n}{\sqrt{5n}} = \frac{0.06\sqrt{n}}{\sqrt{5}}$$

Defining the critical z-value:
$$z = \frac{0.06\sqrt{n}}{\sqrt{5}}$$

## Solving for $n$

We need:
$$P(-z \leqslant Z \leqslant z) \geqslant 0.5 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad 2\Phi(z)-1 \geqslant 0.5 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \Phi(z)\geqslant 0.75$$

This gives:
$$z \geqslant \Phi^{-1}(0.75) \approx 0.6745$$

Solving:
$$\frac{0.06\sqrt{n}}{\sqrt{5}} \geqslant 0.6745$$

$$\sqrt{n} \geqslant \frac{0.6745\sqrt{5}}{0.06} = \frac{0.6745 \times 2.2361}{0.06} = \frac{1.5083}{0.06} \approx 25.14$$

$$n \geqslant 25.14^2 \approx 632$$

## Verification

| $n$ | $z = \frac{0.06\sqrt{n}}{\sqrt{5}}$ | $P = 2\Phi(z)-1$ | Satisfies? |
|-----|--------------------------------------|-------------------|------------|
| 631 | 0.6740 | ≈ 0.4994 | ✗ |
| **632** | **0.6746** | **≈ 0.5000** | **✓** |

At $n = 632$, the probability of the desired inequality equals (just reaches) $\frac{1}{2}$, satisfying the "not less than" condition.

$$\boxed{632}$$
